newsitem.title: USA: U.S. meat export reporting proposal due soon.
newsitem.headline: U.S. meat export reporting proposal due soon.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department hopes to publish its initial proposal for reporting of meat export sales within two weeks, Foreign Agriculture Service Associate Administrator Tim Galvin said Tuesday.
The department was putting the final touches to the proposal before sending it to the Office of Management and Budget for approval, Galvin told Reuters.
"We are hopeful that it will be published in the Federal Register within a couple of weeks," Galvin said.
The proposal stems from Agriculture Department efforts to increase market information about the meat industry and reduce the market power of the major meat processors.
After the department publishes its advance notice of proposed rulemaking, there will be a 60-day public comment period before the department publishes a formal proposed regulation.
Barring significant delays, the final rule should be published around April next year, USDA officials have said.
USDA has said the rule will impose similar export sale reporting requirements on meat as are currently in effect for grains, oilseeds and their products.
